milestone: G2-D security hardening and trust regression remediation

branch_state_at_start.note: The seven owner-observed trust failures were already fixed in 590f67a (pin binding). This milestone keeps that fix, re-expresses changed-identity semantics under the approved F4 design, and hardens the rest of the foundation.

increments.summary: explicit corruption recovery, commit-time validation, typed reset results, retired id guard, adapter exception translation
pin/observed/previous separation, strict trust record codec with invariants, terminal idempotent peer revocation, evidence-based labels
G2dPlatformKeyCapabilities injected into the service, capability checks at create/rotate/load, insecure-store construction guard
serialized mutations, rotation-history invariant, hasVerifiedProtection semantics, documented probe-claim boundary, alias/provider validation, adapter failure tests

notes.F11: The key handle constructor cannot verify a probe result, and tests need to construct invalid handles to prove rejection. The boundary is now documented, and the claim is enforced at decode, lifecycle and platform layers.
notes.F16: Closed by the same commit-time round-trip introduced for F2; the double's unvalidated save is now harmless because nothing reaches it without validation.
notes.F4_remaining: The record shape changed (observed identity). No peer store exists, so there is no legacy format to migrate; a future store must decode through the strict fromMap, which rejects rather than repairs.

schema_changes.identity_record: unchanged, recordVersion 1; new invariants only (pending rotation protection, revocation time ordering, rotated generation must name its predecessor, alias/fingerprint separation)
schema_changes.peer_trust_record: adds observedIdentityFingerprint; strict fromMap/toMap, equality and hashCode; revoked tombstones may not carry axes, a pin, a pending change or verification facts
schema_changes.migration: none implemented and none claimed; no peer record has ever been persisted

capabilities: platform capability interface injected into the service
pin/observed/previous identity separation with ceremony-only promotion
strict peer trust codec with contradiction rejection
serialized mutations and retired identity ids

not_implemented: real device probe and key generation
durable peer or identity store; durable retired-id tombstone
any UI for identity or trust
dependency, Gradle, Android or G2-C changes

tests.reason: no Dart/Flutter/JDK toolchain in the agent environment

agent_run.dart_syntax_parse: tree-sitter-dart parse of all ten identity files after every increment: no errors

security_gates.note: Hardening code and unit tests do not satisfy any gate. Independent design and code review remain mandatory, and no Keystore adapter, provider integration or device probe exists.

unresolved_limitations: no secure persistence: the shipped store fails closed and persists nothing
retired identity ids are remembered only in memory
protection claims rely on the caller's probe attestation, gated but not proven
device-capability drift is recoverable only through the explicit corrupt reset
peer trust records are in-memory only and have no store
no independent review, no device evidence, no cryptographic provider
next_action: Owner runs flutter analyze / flutter test / flutter build apk --debug at the pushed head. No G2-D integration work until D2-a/D2-b gates are answered.

keystore_milestone.milestone: G2-D Android Keystore adapter and persistent identity storage
keystore_milestone.note: Supersedes the 'no Keystore adapter, no secure persistence' limitation recorded in this file by the previous milestone. Identity key generation, a crypto provider, peer trust persistence and every security gate remain open.

increments.summary: Android Keystore wrapping key, AES-GCM envelope, typed failures, measured capability probe, channel client and evidence model
crash-safe encrypted slot storage, Dart store adapter, composition root, backup exclusion
70 Dart cases and 16 instrumented Kotlin tests
G2-D-ANDROID-KEYSTORE-AND-STORAGE.md, key-management doc updates, this state

android_apis: KeyProperties AES/GCM/NoPadding, randomized encryption, no user-auth binding
fullBackupContent (API 23) and dataExtractionRules (API 31, guarded by compileSdk)

protection.wrapping_key: AES-256-GCM, non-exportable, Keystore-chosen iv, no user-authentication binding
protection.envelope: G2DID1 | version | generation | keyId | iv | ciphertext+tag, with version+generation+keyId bound as GCM associated data
protection.atomicity: temporary file, fsync, rename onto one of two alternating slots; the previous generation stays readable
protection.rollback_detection: non-secret keyring.meta index; an authenticating record older than the last committed generation is stale_record
protection.hardware_claim: only from KeyInfo.isInsideSecureHardware of a key this process created; never from the API level

dart.is_secure_at_rest: measured AES-GCM round trip, not a constant
dart.error_mapping: auth_failed/key_missing/key_invalidated/key_id_mismatch/ciphertext_malformed/stale_record -> corrupt; keystore_unavailable/key_generation_failed/io_unavailable/key_unusable and any unknown code -> unavailable (unknown must never enable a destructive reset)
dart.wiring: G2dAndroidIdentityRuntime refuses to assemble the stack when the wrap did not verify; nothing creates an identity at startup

tests.note: No Flutter, Dart, Java or Android toolchain and no device exist here. Nothing in this milestone was executed.

agent_run.dart_syntax_parse: tree-sitter-dart parse of all lib and test Dart files: 0 errors
agent_run.kotlin_brace_balance: all Kotlin sources balanced after comment/string stripping

unresolved_limitations: identity data is unrecoverable when the wrapping key is lost, invalidated or a backup restores the ciphertext alone; the only recovery is the explicit corrupt reset
rollback detection has no anchor outside the app sandbox: an attacker who can write app-private files can delete the index
a rooted device with the app unlocked can use the wrapping key
no identity key is generated, so no record claims hardware_bound; the SM-G610F hardware backing of the wrapping key is unmeasured
retired identity ids are still in-memory only
no independent design or code review; gates D0-D7 remain open
